title: Normalize a Full Name
statement: Given a full name string that may contain extra spaces and mixed casing, return a normalized version where each word starts with an uppercase letter followed by lowercase letters, and extra spaces are removed.
think: What is the task asking? Clean spacing and fix letter casing for each word.
What is the key operation? Process each word and rebuild a normalized result.
What wording signals stand out? Normalize, full name, uppercase, lowercase, extra spaces.
Which pattern fits? Linear Scan over words.
What is the brute force idea? Manual char-by-char state machine.
What is the better/optimal idea? Split words, normalize each, and join them back.
What are the edge cases? Multiple spaces, one word, already normalized input.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(n) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I remove extra spaces, normalize each token, and join them with a single space.
algorithm: Split by spaces removing empty entries
For each word, uppercase first letter and lowercase the rest
Join normalized words with single spaces
interview: I would split the name into non-empty words, normalize the casing of each word, and join them back with single spaces.
ru: Сначала убираем лишние пробелы, потом каждое слово приводим к виду 'Первая буква большая, остальные маленькие'.

important: Forget to lowercase the rest of each word

gaps: Important: string cleanup and word-level processing
Nice to have: explain split-normalize-join pipeline
constraints: Assume words are separated by spaces and letters are alphabetic.
whyThisPattern: This is a Linear Scan over words because each token is processed once and transformed independently.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because no counts are needed.
Not Two Pointers, because positional comparisons are not the main idea.
